title: This Tiny Creature Can Survive Conditions That Would Kill You Instantly
start_frame_prompt: Ultra-photorealistic vertical extreme macro scientific documentary shot of a tardigrade crawling through a thin film of water among moss, translucent body with realistic internal detail, eight stubby legs moving naturally, microscopic depth of field, neutral laboratory illumination, no text, no cartoon styling.
negative_prompt: cute cartoon tardigrade, monster, giant animal, neon glow, infographic, labels, fake space suit, text, watermark, black bars, duplicated legs
narration: This is a tardigrade, an animal smaller than a millimeter. Some species can survive extraordinary extremes, but not by walking around normally in them. When conditions become dangerously dry, a tardigrade can contract into a dormant tun state, losing most of its body water and sharply reducing metabolism. In that protected state, certain tardigrades can tolerate severe dehydration, intense cold and other stresses that would quickly kill a human. They are not indestructible, and survival depends on species, exposure and condition. Their real superpower is temporarily shutting ordinary life almost all the way down.
captions: THIS ANIMAL IS SMALLER THAN A MILLIMETER.
DANGER ARRIVES: IT FORMS A DORMANT TUN.

scenes.prompt: Begin with the exact living tardigrade crawling naturally through water around moss. Camera tracks beside it at true microscopic scale, showing eight legs gripping substrate and realistic body deformation. Water begins receding gradually as the microhabitat dries; no anthropomorphic expression, no giant scale, no fantasy lighting.

Continue on the same tardigrade as dehydration progresses and it physically contracts into a compact tun state. Show body shortening and legs retracting in a biologically plausible sequence while surrounding water film disappears. Camera moves closer without a cut; no instant magical transformation, no shell forming, no cocoon.

Impossible camera enters the same dormant tun while preserving spatial orientation. Show crowded dehydrated cellular interior with membranes and macromolecules stabilized in a glass-like protective state suggested through realistic molecular crowding, not literal glass crystals. Motion becomes extremely subdued to communicate metabolic arrest; no labels, neon molecules or sci-fi energy shields.

Pull back to the intact microscopic tun as the environment undergoes restrained scientific time-compression through severe cold and desiccation. Frost may form around the substrate but the tardigrade remains dormant and structurally intact. Do not depict fire, lava, explosions, open space or universal invulnerability; premium laboratory survival-test realism.

Water returns gradually to the same moss microhabitat. The same tun rehydrates and slowly expands; legs emerge and the tardigrade resumes crawling. Camera tracks alongside the recovered animal and ends on a crisp living macro shot. Recovery must be gradual and physically coherent, no resurrection flash, no duplicated animal, no generated text.

production_notes.director_intent: Reject the superhero cliché. The visual twist is that survival comes from entering a nearly inactive tun, then recovering when water returns.
production_notes.science_guard: Do not claim all tardigrades survive every extreme or are immortal/indestructible. Survival varies by species, life state, duration and exposure; emphasize cryptobiosis and dehydration tolerance.
production_notes.sound_design: Natural narration; microscopic water and moss ambience kept subtle, near-silence during tun state, gentle return of water sound during recovery; no sci-fi effects.
